episodes.dominant_concept: Constituent Assembly debates & Due Process rejection
A.K. Gopalan case & literalist statutory interpretation

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

MEANING.evidence: Article 21 extends universally to citizens and foreign nationals alike... personal liberty under Article 21

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Drafting Committee deliberately rejected 'due process' and adopted 'procedure established by law'

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Fundamental Rights are not isolated islands... Golden Triangle between Article 14, Article 19, and Article 21

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: procedure prescribed by law... cannot be arbitrary, fanciful, or oppressive. It must satisfy the test of fairness, reasonableness, and natural justice under Article 14

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras in 1950... Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India in 1978... impounded under Section 10(3)(c)

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: Article 21 does not grant an absolute, unrestrained immunity. Where a valid statutory law exists... personal liberty may be constitutionally regulated

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: wellspring from which countless unenumerated rights later flowed... Puttaswamy judgment (mentioned in passing)

concept_units: Matrix as vector transformation function
Eigenvector definition (invariant directional scaling: Ax = lambda x)
Geometric examples (projection lambda=1,0; reflection; 90-deg rotation lambda=+-i)
Characteristic equation det(A - lambda I) = 0 via singular nullspace requirement
Characteristic polynomial expansion and root solving
Trace and determinant invariant checks
Eigenvector solution via singular (A - lambda I)x = 0

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: A x = lambda x. The non-zero vector x is called an eigenvector... lambda is the eigenvalue.

MEANING.evidence: multiplying by the matrix does not change the vector's direction; it only scales it by some constant number lambda.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: (A - lambda I) x = 0... matrix must be singular! And a matrix is singular if and only if its determinant is zero.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: We are looking for an eigenvector x that is NOT the zero vector... non-zero vector x in the nullspace of (A - lambda I).

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: 90-degree rotation matrix... no real vector can stay parallel... eigenvalues are imaginary, plus and minus i.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: factor A = S Lambda S^-1 and compute powers of matrices (mentioned in preview)

concept_units: Breadth-First Search ripple analogy & level-order definition
FIFO Queue requirement vs LIFO Stack (DFS distinction)
Queue invariant (non-decreasing distance, at most two consecutive levels d and d+1)
Visited array/set invariant (cycle prevention, duplicate avoidance)
5-node graph step-by-step execution trace
Computational complexity O(V + E) and space O(V)
Disconnected graph limitation

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: Breadth-First Search, or BFS... First-In, First-Out. That is why Breadth-First Search strictly requires a FIFO Queue.

MEANING.evidence: Ripples expand outward uniformly in concentric circles... visits vertices in order of their distance from S.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Queue: Q = [A]... Visited boolean array or hash set... adjacency list

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Queue contains vertices from at most two consecutive levels: d and d+1. All at d are expanded before d+1.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: If we do not mark a vertex as visited, the algorithm would loop infinitely inside a cycle, or enqueue the exact same vertex multiple times.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: Step 1: pop A, enqueue B,C. Step 2: pop B, enqueue D. Step 3: pop C, see D visited. Step 4: pop D, enqueue E. Step 5: pop E.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: If the graph had a disconnected component... this single BFS call would not visit them.

concept_units: Fully connected autoencoder architecture & 2D flattening drawback
Convolutional autoencoder spatial feature learning & limitations
Variational Autoencoder continuous latent space motivation
Probabilistic bottleneck: Gaussian mean (mu) and variance (sigma^2)
Standard Gaussian prior N(0, I) and empty space gaps problem
Loss function decomposition: Reconstruction loss + KL divergence regularizer
Reparameterization trick preview

episodes.dominant_concept: FC vs Conv autoencoders & flattening failure

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: first autoencoder that comes into picture is fully connected autoencoder... third type is Variational Autoencoders, or VAEs

MEANING.evidence: we do not want to look at one fixed point where the data is available. We want to understand the probability distribution of data in the latent space.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: predicting two vectors: the mean (mu) of the data distribution, and the variance (sigma squared) of the data distribution.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: loss function of a VAE has two components: First, reconstruction loss... Second, the KL divergence... which acts as a regularizer

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: If we do not regularize, the network will simply set variance to zero and push classes infinitely far apart... empty gaps where sampling produces gibberish.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: predicting Gaussian parameters for image pixel compression

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: main reason why fully connected autoencoders fail is because the 2D dimension of image is directly flattened, losing all spatial neighborhood

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: reparameterization trick allows backpropagation through random sampling (mentioned in closing)

concept_units: Law of Demand vs Price Elasticity concept (responsiveness magnitude)
Percentage change definition Ed = (% change Q) / (% change P)
Unit-free comparison justification
Base dependency problem & Midpoint Formula solution
Numerical worked calculation (price $10->$14, quantity 100->60, |Ed|=1.50)
Elastic (|Ed|>1), inelastic (|Ed|<1), and unit elastic (|Ed|=1) classification
Total Revenue Test (TR = P * Q; inelastic vs elastic revenue consequences)
Consumer surplus & Deadweight Loss triangle from price ceiling

episodes.dominant_concept: Law of Demand vs Price Elasticity concept

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: price elasticity of demand, which we denote as E_d

MEANING.evidence: degree of responsiveness is what we measure through elasticity... percentage change in quantity demanded divided by percentage change in price

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Total revenue is Price times Quantity: TR = P * Q... If demand is inelastic, quantity effect is small... TR increases. If elastic, TR falls.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: Percentages make elasticity unit-free... Midpoint resolves base-dependency problem.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: price $10 to $14, quantity 100 to 60... percentage Q is -50%, percentage P is +33.3%... E_d = -1.50, absolute value is 1.50.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: binding price ceiling below market equilibrium... lost social surplus that benefits no one is Deadweight Loss triangle

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: tax incidence depends directly on relative elasticities (mentioned in preview)
